mathematics_checks: The literal real unit sphere is S={-1,1}. The chord is |1-(-1)|=2, and the real inner product is -1 so the angular cost is arccos(-1)=pi; arccos(1)=0 on the diagonal. The subspace topology is discrete, hence both S and its product have all subsets Borel and both squared costs are measurable.

A continuous sphere-valued path from 1 to -1 would give a continuous real function on [0,1] with the same endpoints, hence would hit 0. No continuous path exists, so there are no rectifiable paths to minimize over and the extended path cost, and its square, are +infinity at the antipodes. A constant path handles the diagonal; an ambient straight line through 0 is inadmissible.

A feasible gamma has gamma({1}×S)=gamma(S×{-1})=1 by its respective marginals. Both complements have mass zero, so their intersection { (1,-1) } has mass one. Conversely the Dirac measure at (1,-1) has the required marginals, proving existence and uniqueness without assuming that feasible couplings are independent.

The extended integral at the unique Dirac plan is the cost evaluated at (1,-1), giving raw values pi^2 and +infinity, not square-root distances. The transport infimum is over a singleton in both cases; only the antipodal path infimum is empty. For any probability marginals their product is feasible and c^2 <= pi^2 pointwise, so pi^2 is a uniform angular transport bound. The computed Dirac pair rules out the corresponding finite intrinsic bound; this is a change of cost, not nonattainment or failure of coupling feasibility.

mathematics_checks: On the full binary sigma algebra, the deterministic second-call rules define Markov kernels x↦delta_x and x↦delta_0 for both x=0 and x=1, even at zero-mass histories. H0 implements both calls, H1 idealizes just the first, and H2 idealizes both. Their Y-only laws are respectively Ber(q), Ber(p), and delta_0=Ber(0). The first adjacent pair shares the identity suffix.

The empty and full events give zero difference, and the singleton discrepancies for Ber(a) and Ber(b) are a-b and b-a. The event-supremum TV is therefore |a-b| with no extra factor. The adjacent gaps are |q-p| and p. At the second replacement the local TV is 1_{x=1}; both H1 and H2 reach that slot with history Ber(p), under which the mean is exactly p. The local budget is measurable and integrable without any version or support issue.

The actual endpoint TV is q. The triangle telescope gives q <= |q-p|+p; the excess is zero if q>=p and 2(p-q)>0 otherwise, so tightness holds exactly for q>=p, including all applicable degenerate endpoints and q=p.

Using Ber(q) gives the numerical budget q but changes the averaging law for the fixed H1,H2 pair. At p=3/4 and q=1/4, the actual second gap is 3/4, so 3/4 <= 1/4 is false. The substituted total |q-p|+q is 3/4 there and still dominates the actual endpoint 1/4; indeed it dominates q for every admissible p,q. A different replacement order would require a different adjacent pair and a newly checked common history.
